content:
I have a working prototype of a @[norm_num] extension for real valued transcendental bounds. It closes things like

lean
example : (2718 : ℝ) / 1000 < Real.exp 1 := by norm_num
example : Real.log (2 : ℝ) < 694 / 1000 := by norm_num
example : -(694 : ℝ) / 1000 < Real.log (1/2) := by norm_num
example : (968 : ℝ) / 1000 < Real.cos (1/4) := by norm_num

bounds are Taylor-Lagrange; the extension tries increasing degree (n = 5, 7, 9,...) until the polynomial sum clears the target. Covers exp(r), exp(-r), log(r) (r > 1 and r in (0,1)), sin(r), cos(r) for rational r in the approp ranges.

I also checked out Geoffrey Irving's interval tactic (standalone and based on native_decide; not @[norm_num]) and LeanCert (alerad/leancert, handles ∀ x ∈ I, f(x) ≤ c for symbolic x, also not @[norm_num]). This prototype hooks into norm_num dispatch; all proof terms are kernel-checked with no native_decide (axioms: {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound}).

I scanned Mathlib/Tactic/NormNum and found nothing for transcendental functions, but I may have missed something.

q0: Is there existing @[norm_num] support for Real.exp or similar?

this prototype works by calling existing tactics via evalTactic + TermElabM.run', which is not how Mathlib NormNum extensions are usually structured.

for a proper PR the bound computation would have to move into MetaM if im right:

  • compute the partial sum as a rational
  • call normNumDischarge for comparison

q1: Is there a good worked example of a NormNum extension that constructs a numeric value in MetaM rather than just pattern matching on the expression?

one issue I encountered: when the n-term partial sum S_n = ∑_{k<n} r^k/k! does not yet exceed a, the inner norm_num call trying to prove a < S_n does not throw. Instead it reduces the goal to ⊢ False (by proving the negation) and leaves it unsolved. Then done throws. Somewhere in the eval machinery (I suspect a withLogging wrapper inside evalTactic) gets written to message log before propagating out. The outer try/catch catches the exception, but the log entry is already there. If a later degree succeeds, the build still reports an error from the failed attempt.

fix i applied: Core.getMessageLog / Core.setMessageLog around each attempt.

q2: Is this the standard pattern for suppressing tactic noise during backtracking or is there something cleaner?

prototype: https://github.com/peti12352/interval-decide
IIRC, interval arithmetic is a wanted feature but I don't think we would want to extend norm_num for it. It would probably be its own tactic with its own extensibility.
This is pretty neat that you can make norm_num do this though!
There's previous discussion at #mathlib4 > norm_num extensions (and a few other topics)
thanks for the input! checked them out, the extensibility is pretty valid one; i will probably consider implementing it as the standalone tactic
